notes.text:
All Israel — Namely, their representatives. Shechem - To the city of Shechem, a place convenient for the purpose, not only because it was a Levitical city, and a city of refuge, and a place near Joshua's city, but especially for the two main ends for which he summoned them thither.

1. For the solemn burial of the bones of Joseph, and the rest of the patriarchs, for which this place was designed.

2. For the solemn renewing of their covenant with God; which in this place was first made between God and Abraham, Gen. xii, 6, 7, and afterwards renewed by the Israelites at their first entrance into the land of Canaan, between the two mountains of Ebal and Gerizzim, chap. viii, 30, &c. which were very near Shechem: and therefore this place was most proper, both to remind them of their former obligations to God, and to engage them to a farther ratification of them. Before God - As in God's presence, to hear what Joshua was to speak to them in God's name, and to receive God's commands from his mouth. He had taken a solemn farewell before: but as God renewed his strength, he desired to improve it for their good. We must never think our work for God done, 'till our life is done.

The people — To the elders, by whom it was to be imparted to all the rest, and to as many of the people as came thither. He spake to them in God's name, and as from him, in the language of a prophet, Thus saith the Lord. Jehovah, the great God, and the God of Israel, whom you are peculiarly engaged to hear. The flood - Or, the river, namely, Euphrates, so called by way of eminency. They served - That is, Both Abraham and Nahor were no less idolaters than the rest of mankind. This is said to prevent their vain boasting in their worthy ancestors, and to assure them that whatsoever good was in, or had been done by their progenitors, was wholly from God's free grace, and not for their own merit or righteousness.

I took — I snatched him out of that idolatrous place, and took him into acquaintance and covenant with myself, which was the highest honour and happiness he was capable of. And led - That is I brought him after his father's death into Canaan, Gen. xii, 1, and I conducted and preserved him in all his travels through the several parts of Canaan. And multiplied - That is, gave him a numerous posterity, not only by Hagar and Keturah, but even by Sarah and by Isaac. Gave Isaac - By my special power and grace to be heir of my covenant, and all my promises, and the seed in or by which all the nations were to be blessed.

The gods — Whereby it appears, that although Joshua had doubtless prevented and purged out all public idolatry, yet there were some of them who practiced it in their private houses and retirements. Your fathers - Terah, and Nahor, and Abraham, as ver. 2, and other of your ancestors. In Egypt - See Ezek xxiii, 3, 8, 19, 21, 27. Under these particulars, no doubt he comprehends all other false gods, which were served by the nations amongst whom they were, but only mentions these, as the idols which they were in more danger of worshipping than those in Canaan; partly because those of Canaan had been now lately and palpably disgraced by their inability to preserve their worshippers from total ruin; and partly, because the other idols came recommended to them by the venerable name of antiquity, and the custom of their forefathers.

Seem evil — Unjust, unreasonable or inconvenient. Choose ye - Not that he leaves them to their liberty, whether they would serve God or idols; for Joshua had no such power himself, nor could give it to any other; and both he and they were obliged by the law of Moses, to give their worship to God only, and to forbear all idolatry in themselves, and severely to punish it in others; but it is a powerful insinuation, whereby he both implies, that the worship of God is so highly reasonable, necessary and beneficial; and the service of idols so absurd, and vain, and pernicious, that if it were left free for all men to take their choice, every man in his right wits must needs chuse the service of God, before that of idols; and provokes them to bind themselves faster to God by their own choice. He will - But know this, if you should all be so base and brutish, as to prefer senseless and impotent idols, before the true and living God, it is my firm purpose, that I will, and my children, and servants (as far as I can influence them) shall be constant and faithful to the Lord. And that, whatever others do. They that resolve to serve God, must not start at being singular in it. They that are bound for heaven must be willing to swim against the stream, and must do, not as most do, but as the best do.

Ye cannot — He speaks not of an absolute impossibility, (for then both his resolution to serve God himself, and his exhortation to them had been vain) but of a moral impossibility, or a very great difficulty, which he alledgeth not to discourage them from God's service, but to make them more considerate in obliging themselves; and more resolved in answering their obligations. The meaning is, God's service is not, as you seem to fancy, a slight and easy thing, but it is a work of great difficulty, and requires great care, and courage and resolution; and when I consider the infinite purity of God, that he will not be mocked or abused; and withal your proneness to superstition and idolatry, even during the life of Moses, and in some of you, while I live, and while the obligations which God had laid upon you in this land, are fresh in remembrance; I cannot but fear that after my decease you will think the service of God burdensome, and therefore will cast it off and revolt from him, if you do not carefully avoid all occasions of idolatry. A jealous God - In the Hebrew, He is the holy Gods, holy Father, holy Son, holy Spirit. He will not endure a partner in his worship; you can not serve him and idols together. Will not forgive - If you who own yourselves his people and servants, shall wilfully transgress his laws, he will not let this go unpunished in you, as he doth in other nations; therefore consider what you do, when you take the Lord for your God; weigh your advantages and inconveniences together; for as if you be sincere and faithful in God's service, you will have admirable benefits by it; so if you be false to your professions, and forsake him whom you have so solemnly avouched to be your God, he will deal more severely with you than with any people in the world.

Will turn — That is, he will alter his course and the manner of his dealing with you, and will be as severe as ever he was kind and gracious. He will repent of his former kindnesses, and his goodness abused will be turned into fury.
The Lord — Namely, him only, and not strange gods.
Against yourselves — This solemn profession will be a swift witness against you, if hereafter you apostatize from God.

Strange gods — Those idols which you either brought out of Egypt, or have taken in Canaan, which some of you keep contrary to God's command, whether for the preciousness of the matter, or rather for some secret inclination to superstition and idolatry.
A statute — He set or established that covenant with them, that is, the people, for a statute or an ordinance, to bind themselves and their posterity unto God forever.

glossa.text: *I took therefore your father.* ((AUG.)) In that the LXX have, etc., *as far as* which is the true seed of Abraham.

*You shall not be able. ((AUG., quaest. 28 in Jos.))* You shall not be able to serve the Lord, etc., *as far as* and afterwards grace might more abound through Jesus Christ, who is the end of the law.

*Take away. ((AUG., quaest. 29 in Jos.))* What is it that he says, etc., *as far as: face to face we may know him ((I Cor. XIII))*.

*((AUG., quaest. 30 in Jos.)) And Jesus ordained a testament,* etc. They who search these words more deeply, etc., *as far as: but all forsook me, which let it not be laid to their charge ((II Tim. IV))*.

notes.text: My law — The doctrine which I am about to deliver. 2. Parable - Weighty sentences. Dark sayings - Not that the words are hard to be understood, but the things, God's transcendent goodness, their unparallel'd ingratitude; and their stupid ignorance and insensibleness, under such excellent teachings of God's word and works, are prodigious and hard to be believed. Of old - Of things done in ancient times.

Established — This is justly put in first place, as the chief of all his mercies. A testimony - His law, called a testimony, because it is a witness between God and men, declaring the duties which God expects from man, and the blessings which man may expect from God.

glossa.text: *Understanding.* ((AUG.)) Because these things narrated, etc., *as far as* the things that seem open are parables and riddles. *Attend.* ((CAS.)) First the Lord himself speaks, that reverence may grow. *My people,* who obey me. The mouth of God is Asaph, who spoke these things below: *How great things we have heard from the beginning.* Of the Old Testament: or, the faithful Synagogue reproaches the wicked.
*In parables.* ((AUG.)) Parables are likenesses of things. *Propositions.* Which in Greek are *problemata,* questions having something to be resolved.

*How great things.* ((CAS.)) He tells summarily what God did for the Jews: yet for men ungrateful to him, and thus, if not to them, it profits the sons nevertheless, lest they become as their fathers. ((AUG.)) First God spoke in a man, now the man himself: *How great things we have heard.* That foretold word God spoke from himself, lest his speech be despised.

*And he raised up,* etc. ((AUG.)) This testimony. *The beginning,* whence above: *I will utter propositions from the beginning.* The beginning is the Old Testament, the end the New. There is fear, which is the beginning: but here is Christ, *the end of the law unto righteousness to every one that believeth ((Rom. X))*, who gives the Spirit, whence: *Charity, which drives out fear ((I Joan. IV))* . The old law is called the testimony of this New Testament, because it has testimony from the law and the Prophets: whence that was called the tabernacle of testimony which prefigured so many mystical things: *Testimony* therefore the Old Testament is called in so far as it proves and testifies, law in so far as it commands. ((CASS., REM.)) *He raised up* the testimony as though dead in Adam, that is, the law; or, while it is written down it is raised up, having been lulled asleep before by ignorance. *A testimony in Jacob,* this perhaps is that Jacob, having wrestled with the angel, went halt when his thigh was touched: which signifies that the Jews partly stand fast in faith, partly depart from salvation: and so what befell Jacob was a testimony of this thing. Behold a parable. *To their sons.* And these same sons are another generation, namely the people of grace.
*Another generation.* Through the generations the commandments of God were handed on, lest any think them given to one only.

*That they may set.* This is the profit of the fathers' preaching. *Let them seek out.* ((AUG.)) Those who were said above to have known, now *let them seek out,* that hoping in God they may be helped by him to fulfil it.

notes.text: Now — Herein the efficacy of Christianity greatly appears, - that it neither takes away nor embitters, but sweetly tempers, that most refined of all affections, our desire of or love to the dead.
So — As God raised him. With him - With their living head.

By the word of the Lord — By a particular Revelation. We who are left - This intimates the fewness of those who will be then alive, compared to the multitude of the dead. Believers of all ages and nations make up, as it were, one body; in consideration of which, the believers of that age might put themselves in the place, and speak in the person, of them who were to live till the coming of the Lord. Not that St. Paul hereby asserted (though some seem to have imagined so) that the day of the Lord was at hand.

With a shout — Properly, a proclamation made to a great multitude. Above this is, the voice of the archangel; above both, the trumpet of God; the voice of God, somewhat analogous to the sound of a trumpet.
Together — In the same moment. In the air - The wicked will remain beneath, while the righteous, being absolved, shall be assessors with their Lord in the judgment. With the Lord - In heaven.

glossa.text: *Through Jesus will he bring with him.* Ever going on, by following him they came to the sleep of death, whence also it is written in another Epistle: *We who live.*

*Them.* Not only those who shall be found alive, but also the dead, concerning whom you doubt. *Who have slept.* He calls Christ dead, the faithful sleeping, that they may the more believe the resurrection: he calls Christ dead, that when we have heard that he died and rose again, we also may hope that we shall rise again through the power of his divinity.

*For the Lord himself.* In his own person.

*With the trumpet of God. ((ANSELM.))* This trumpet will rouse all and will terrify the enemies, will summon his own to battle, that they may vanquish the adversaries, and that [the adversaries] may flee from the face of the Lord and be sent into hell. And again, as the trumpet once called together the people of the Hebrews on the feasts: so this trumpet will call together the people of the saints to the solemnity of eternal gladness, God, he says, commanding, and with the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God sounding. *He shall descend.* Not lowly as before, but commanding with a voice, either his own or the archangel's, or the angels', by which he will make the dead rise again, which is called a trumpet, because it is manifest, or as though for battle, which shall be God's and Christ's, to which God will give efficacy.
*In the clouds.* Because a cloud will take them up, as it took up Christ at the ascension, whence another interpreter says: *With bearing clouds.*

notes.text: Then shall the kingdom of heaven — That is, the candidates for it, be like ten virgins - The bridemaids on the wedding night were wont to go to the house where the bride was, with burning lamps or torches in their hands, to wait for the bride groom's coming. When he drew near, they went to meet him with their lamps, and to conduct him to the bride.

The foolish took no oil with them — No more than kept them burning just for the present. None to supply their future want, to recruit their lamp's decay. The lamp is faith. A lamp and oil with it, is faith working by love.
The wise took oil in their vessels — Love in their hearts. And they daily sought a fresh supply of spiritual strength, till their faith was made perfect.
While the bridegroom delayed — That is, before they were called to attend him, they all slumbered and slept - Were easy and quiet, the wise enjoying a true, the foolish a false peace.
At midnight — In an hour quite unthought of.
They trimmed their lamps — They examined themselves and prepared to meet their God.

Give us of your oil, for our lamps are gone out — Our faith is dead. What a time to discover this! Whether it mean the time of death, or of judgment. Unto which of the saints wilt thou then turn? Who can help thee at such a season?

But the wise answered, Lest there be not enough for us and you! — Beginning the sentence with a beautiful abruptness; such as showed their surprise at the state of those poor wretches, who had so long received them, as well as their own souls. Lest there be not enough - It is sure there is not; for no man has more than holiness enough for himself. Go ye rather to them that sell - Without money and without price: that is, to God, to Christ. And buy - If ye can. O no! The time is past and returns no more!
Watch therefore — He that watches has not only a burning lamp, but likewise oil in his vessel. And even when he sleepeth, his heart waketh. He is quiet; but not secure.

glossa.text: *Ten virgins.* The virgins are all who refrain themselves from the luxury of the world. *And the bride.* All together are the bride, who has now been espoused a virgin away from the corruption of the world. She shall be wedded, when the mortal shall be joined to the immortal.
*Five.* Because continence in carnal enticements is fivefold, namely that in the five senses they should refrain themselves from pleasures.
*And the bridegroom tarrying.* Because there is no little time between the first and the second coming of Christ. *They all slumbered and slept.* Because they are afterwards to be raised up.
*And at midnight there was a cry made.* That is, with no one knowing or hoping for it. Whence *The day of the Lord shall come as a thief in the night ((I Thess. III))*.

*Give us of your oil,* etc. Those whose deeds are propped up by what is another's fail when that same praise is withdrawn, and out of habit they always seek that whence the mind is wont to rejoice. And so they wish to have before God, who is the searcher of the heart, the testimony of men, who do not see hearts.

*They are going out.* That is, at the coming of the judge they are darkened within, and they have no reward from God, because they have received their praise.

*Lest perhaps.* Because each shall render an account for himself, nor is anyone helped before God by another's testimony, since to him secret things lie open, and each scarcely suffices for himself, that his own conscience may bear him witness. *Lest perhaps* each one shall receive a reward for his own works, nor in the day of judgment can the virtues of some relieve the vices of others. *To them that sell.* They that sell are flatterers, because they give praise and receive some reward.

*But whilst.* While they bend themselves toward the things that are without, and seek their accustomed joys, since they have not known the things within, he comes who judges. *It was shut.* After the judgment great is the severity of him whose mercy before it is unspeakable.

*But last of all.* By true penance, by fruitless tears, those left outside knock. It is not said that they bought oil: because, no joy from the praises of others now remaining, in their straits they return to the imploring of God.

*Watch ye.* Namely, that we may prepare for ourselves the testimony of a good conscience, lest with the foolish virgins we remain outside. *You know not the day nor the hour.* Not only the day of judgment, but the day of each man's death, or the hour in which he who is found ready shall then also be found ready. And because he desires to find us ready, he adds another parable on the same matter.

places.name: Shechem
places.id: Tell Balata at the eastern edge of modern Nablus, in the saddle between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. The patriarchal sanctuary of Gen 12:6, 33:18-20 and the covenant-renewal site of Joshua 24. Excavations by Sellin and Wright revealed Middle and Late Bronze fortifications and a fortress-temple.

places.name: The River
places.id: The Euphrates, called simply 'the River' in Hebrew. The eastern frontier of the patriarchal homeland (Ur of the Chaldees and Haran lay beyond it) and the ideal northeastern boundary of the promised land (Gen 15:18, Josh 1:4). Pin sits on the middle Euphrates near ancient Mari.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book. Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
echoes.note: The promise that at the end 'many who sleep in the dust shall awake' grounds Paul's hope for 'those who have fallen asleep' rising. The deliverance of God's people and the resurrection/awakening sequence is the clearest scriptural matrix for vv. 14-16.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: Being 'caught up together... in the clouds, to meet the Lord' draws on the vision of one like a son of man coming 'with the clouds of heaven.' The cloud imagery of glorious eschatological encounter is Danielic.

echoes.text: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled. Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the lower part of the mountain. Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked […]
echoes.note: The Sinai theophany, with the LORD descending, thick cloud, and a very loud trumpet blast, supplies the template for the Lord descending from heaven with God's trumpet and a shout. Paul recasts covenant theophany as parousia.

echoes.text: Yahweh will be seen over them; and his arrow will go flash like lightning; and the Lord Yahweh will blow the trumpet, and will go with whirlwinds of the south.
echoes.note: 'the Lord GOD will sound the trumpet' as the divine warrior appears closely matches 'with God's trumpet' at the Lord's descent. The eschatological trumpet of divine advent is shared.

echoes.text: Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.
echoes.note: 'Your dead shall live... awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust' is a primary OT resurrection text behind 'the dead in Christ will rise.' The awakening of the dead at the LORD's coming directly informs Paul's hope against grief.

echoes.text: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of Yahweh comes, for it is close at hand:
echoes.note: 'Blow the trumpet in Zion... for the day of the LORD is coming' associates the trumpet blast with the day of the Lord, the framework for Paul's trumpet and parousia. Continues into 1 Thess 5's 'day of the Lord.'

echoes.text: It will happen in that day that a great trumpet will be blown; and those who were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and those who were outcasts in the land of Egypt, shall come; and they will worship Yahweh in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
echoes.note: 'a great trumpet will be blown' to gather the scattered to worship the LORD parallels the trumpet summoning the dead and living to meet the Lord. Eschatological-gathering trumpet motif.

echoes.text: For, behold, Yahweh comes out of his place, and will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
echoes.note: 'the LORD is coming forth out of his place, and will come down' provides the descent imagery of God leaving heaven to act, echoed in 'the Lord himself will descend from heaven.' Theophanic descent.

echoes.text: God has gone up with a shout, Yahweh with the sound of a trumpet.
echoes.note: 'God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet' uniquely pairs a loud shout with a trumpet blast, the precise combination in 'with a shout... and with God's trumpet.' Direction is reversed (ascent vs. descent) but the acclamation imagery is striking.

echoes.text: You shall flee by the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach to Azel; yes, you shall flee, just like you fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Yahweh my God will come, and all the holy ones with you./f + Septuagint reads “him” instead of “you”./f*
echoes.note: 'the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him' parallels 'God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep' and the Lord's coming accompanied by his people. Often cited behind the parousia retinue.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying, “Make two trumpets of silver. You shall make them of beaten work. You shall use them for the calling of the congregation, and for the journeying of the camps. When they blow them, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the door of the Tent of Meeting. If they blow just one, then the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather themselves to you. When you blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the […]
echoes.note: The silver trumpets that summon the assembly and signal God's remembrance offer a cultic backdrop to the eschatological trumpet gathering the saints. Faint and thematic.

echoes.text: a day of the trumpet and alarm, against the fortified cities, and against the high battlements.
echoes.note: 'a day of trumpet blast' for the day of the LORD reinforces the trumpet-of-judgment-and-advent motif. Faint, part of the cluster of day-of-the-LORD trumpet texts.

echoes.text: As they still went on, and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
echoes.note: Elijah's being 'taken up' bodily to heaven, like Enoch (Gen 5:24), figurally anticipates the living being 'caught up' to meet the Lord without death. Typological rather than verbal.

echoes.text: Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.
echoes.note: Enoch, who 'was not, for God took him,' prefigures the rapture of the living to be with the Lord forever. Faint figural precedent for translation without death.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons shall marry you; and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
echoes.note: The bridegroom motif organizing the whole parable draws on the prophetic image of God/Messiah as bridegroom: 'as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.' Matthew makes the coming bridegroom the figure for the returning Son of Man, joining the eschatological wedding feast to messianic arrival.

echoes.text: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion. I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Yahweh.
echoes.note: God's betrothal of Israel ('I will betroth you to me forever') stands behind the bridegroom-and-attendants imagery; the marriage covenant is the controlling metaphor for the eschatological union the wise virgins enter and the foolish miss.

echoes.text: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant? Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel. They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night. King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon. He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of […]
echoes.note: The nocturnal coming of the bridegroom in procession, the cry going up, and the wedding of King Solomon supply a scriptural scene of a bridegroom arriving by night to be met by attendants. Verbal contact is thematic rather than lexical.

echoes.text: “Woe to you who desire the day of Yahweh! Why do you long for the day of Yahweh? It is darkness, and not light. As if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him; Or he went into the house and leaned his hand on the wall, and a snake bit him. Won’t the day of Yahweh be darkness, and not light? Even very dark, and no brightness in it?
echoes.note: The reversal whereby those who presume entry are shut out ('Lord, Lord, open to us' / 'I don't know you') resonates with the prophetic Day of the LORD warning that the day will be darkness for the complacent, not the light they expected.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies. “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap;
echoes.note: 'The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple... but who can endure the day of his coming?' supplies the pattern of a sudden, testing arrival of the Lord for which one must be prepared; the delay-then-sudden-cry structure of the parable echoes this.

echoes.text: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
echoes.note: 'Though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not delay' frames the theme of the bridegroom's delay (v.5) and the call to keep ready through the apparent postponement of the appointed time.
echoes.lxxText: For the vision is yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.

echoes.text: “You shall command the children of Israel, that they bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually. In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before Yahweh: it shall be a statute forever throughout their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.
echoes.note: The provision of pure oil to keep the lamp burning continually 'from evening to morning' supplies the cultic background for oil-as-fidelity that keeps the light alive through the night of waiting.

echoes.text: The princess inside is all glorious. Her clothing is interwoven with gold. She shall be led to the king in embroidered work. The virgins, her companions who follow her, shall be brought to you. With gladness and rejoicing they shall be led. They shall enter into the king’s palace.
echoes.note: The royal wedding psalm, with virgin companions led in procession to the king's palace amid gladness, provides a scriptural template for virgins escorting a bridegroom into the marriage feast.

glossa.text: *Love them,* etc., *and you shall have discipline.* He that loves wisdom keeps discipline in his manners. For he does not love wisdom who does not keep discipline. Whence: *If you love me, keep my commandments ((Joan. XIV))*.
*She preventeth them that covet her.* Offering herself freely. For he himself is *the way, the truth, and the life ((Joan. XIV))*: through him one goes, unto him one strives, to him one attains.

*Her sitting by,* etc. Ever ready, that is, to help, whence: *Behold, I stand at the door and knock, if any man shall open to me, I will go in to him and will sup with him, and he with me ((Apoc. III))* . In the present life wisdom must be studied, and life led according to the rule of her discipline.

notes.text: Now — Herein the efficacy of Christianity greatly appears, - that it neither takes away nor embitters, but sweetly tempers, that most refined of all affections, our desire of or love to the dead.
So — As God raised him. With him - With their living head.

By the word of the Lord — By a particular Revelation. We who are left - This intimates the fewness of those who will be then alive, compared to the multitude of the dead. Believers of all ages and nations make up, as it were, one body; in consideration of which, the believers of that age might put themselves in the place, and speak in the person, of them who were to live till the coming of the Lord. Not that St. Paul hereby asserted (though some seem to have imagined so) that the day of the Lord was at hand.

With a shout — Properly, a proclamation made to a great multitude. Above this is, the voice of the archangel; above both, the trumpet of God; the voice of God, somewhat analogous to the sound of a trumpet.
Together — In the same moment. In the air - The wicked will remain beneath, while the righteous, being absolved, shall be assessors with their Lord in the judgment. With the Lord - In heaven.

glossa.text: *Through Jesus will he bring with him.* Ever going on, by following him they came to the sleep of death, whence also it is written in another Epistle: *We who live.*

*Them.* Not only those who shall be found alive, but also the dead, concerning whom you doubt. *Who have slept.* He calls Christ dead, the faithful sleeping, that they may the more believe the resurrection: he calls Christ dead, that when we have heard that he died and rose again, we also may hope that we shall rise again through the power of his divinity.

*For the Lord himself.* In his own person.

*With the trumpet of God. ((ANSELM.))* This trumpet will rouse all and will terrify the enemies, will summon his own to battle, that they may vanquish the adversaries, and that [the adversaries] may flee from the face of the Lord and be sent into hell. And again, as the trumpet once called together the people of the Hebrews on the feasts: so this trumpet will call together the people of the saints to the solemnity of eternal gladness, God, he says, commanding, and with the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God sounding. *He shall descend.* Not lowly as before, but commanding with a voice, either his own or the archangel's, or the angels', by which he will make the dead rise again, which is called a trumpet, because it is manifest, or as though for battle, which shall be God's and Christ's, to which God will give efficacy.
*In the clouds.* Because a cloud will take them up, as it took up Christ at the ascension, whence another interpreter says: *With bearing clouds.*

notes.text: Then shall the kingdom of heaven — That is, the candidates for it, be like ten virgins - The bridemaids on the wedding night were wont to go to the house where the bride was, with burning lamps or torches in their hands, to wait for the bride groom's coming. When he drew near, they went to meet him with their lamps, and to conduct him to the bride.

The foolish took no oil with them — No more than kept them burning just for the present. None to supply their future want, to recruit their lamp's decay. The lamp is faith. A lamp and oil with it, is faith working by love.
The wise took oil in their vessels — Love in their hearts. And they daily sought a fresh supply of spiritual strength, till their faith was made perfect.
While the bridegroom delayed — That is, before they were called to attend him, they all slumbered and slept - Were easy and quiet, the wise enjoying a true, the foolish a false peace.
At midnight — In an hour quite unthought of.
They trimmed their lamps — They examined themselves and prepared to meet their God.

Give us of your oil, for our lamps are gone out — Our faith is dead. What a time to discover this! Whether it mean the time of death, or of judgment. Unto which of the saints wilt thou then turn? Who can help thee at such a season?

But the wise answered, Lest there be not enough for us and you! — Beginning the sentence with a beautiful abruptness; such as showed their surprise at the state of those poor wretches, who had so long received them, as well as their own souls. Lest there be not enough - It is sure there is not; for no man has more than holiness enough for himself. Go ye rather to them that sell - Without money and without price: that is, to God, to Christ. And buy - If ye can. O no! The time is past and returns no more!
Watch therefore — He that watches has not only a burning lamp, but likewise oil in his vessel. And even when he sleepeth, his heart waketh. He is quiet; but not secure.

glossa.text: *Ten virgins.* The virgins are all who refrain themselves from the luxury of the world. *And the bride.* All together are the bride, who has now been espoused a virgin away from the corruption of the world. She shall be wedded, when the mortal shall be joined to the immortal.
*Five.* Because continence in carnal enticements is fivefold, namely that in the five senses they should refrain themselves from pleasures.
*And the bridegroom tarrying.* Because there is no little time between the first and the second coming of Christ. *They all slumbered and slept.* Because they are afterwards to be raised up.
*And at midnight there was a cry made.* That is, with no one knowing or hoping for it. Whence *The day of the Lord shall come as a thief in the night ((I Thess. III))*.

*Give us of your oil,* etc. Those whose deeds are propped up by what is another's fail when that same praise is withdrawn, and out of habit they always seek that whence the mind is wont to rejoice. And so they wish to have before God, who is the searcher of the heart, the testimony of men, who do not see hearts.

*They are going out.* That is, at the coming of the judge they are darkened within, and they have no reward from God, because they have received their praise.

*Lest perhaps.* Because each shall render an account for himself, nor is anyone helped before God by another's testimony, since to him secret things lie open, and each scarcely suffices for himself, that his own conscience may bear him witness. *Lest perhaps* each one shall receive a reward for his own works, nor in the day of judgment can the virtues of some relieve the vices of others. *To them that sell.* They that sell are flatterers, because they give praise and receive some reward.

*But whilst.* While they bend themselves toward the things that are without, and seek their accustomed joys, since they have not known the things within, he comes who judges. *It was shut.* After the judgment great is the severity of him whose mercy before it is unspeakable.

*But last of all.* By true penance, by fruitless tears, those left outside knock. It is not said that they bought oil: because, no joy from the praises of others now remaining, in their straits they return to the imploring of God.

*Watch ye.* Namely, that we may prepare for ourselves the testimony of a good conscience, lest with the foolish virgins we remain outside. *You know not the day nor the hour.* Not only the day of judgment, but the day of each man's death, or the hour in which he who is found ready shall then also be found ready. And because he desires to find us ready, he adds another parable on the same matter.

Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: “At that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince who stands for the children of your people; and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book. Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
echoes.note: The promise that at the end 'many who sleep in the dust shall awake' grounds Paul's hope for 'those who have fallen asleep' rising. The deliverance of God's people and the resurrection/awakening sequence is the clearest scriptural matrix for vv. 14-16.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: Being 'caught up together... in the clouds, to meet the Lord' draws on the vision of one like a son of man coming 'with the clouds of heaven.' The cloud imagery of glorious eschatological encounter is Danielic.

echoes.text: On the third day, when it was morning, there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of an exceedingly loud trumpet; and all the people who were in the camp trembled. Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God; and they stood at the lower part of the mountain. Mount Sinai, all it, smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked […]
echoes.note: The Sinai theophany, with the LORD descending, thick cloud, and a very loud trumpet blast, supplies the template for the Lord descending from heaven with God's trumpet and a shout. Paul recasts covenant theophany as parousia.

echoes.text: Yahweh will be seen over them; and his arrow will go flash like lightning; and the Lord Yahweh will blow the trumpet, and will go with whirlwinds of the south.
echoes.note: 'the Lord GOD will sound the trumpet' as the divine warrior appears closely matches 'with God's trumpet' at the Lord's descent. The eschatological trumpet of divine advent is shared.

echoes.text: Your dead shall live. My dead bodies shall arise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust; for your dew is like the dew of herbs, and the earth will cast out the departed spirits.
echoes.note: 'Your dead shall live... awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust' is a primary OT resurrection text behind 'the dead in Christ will rise.' The awakening of the dead at the LORD's coming directly informs Paul's hope against grief.

echoes.text: Blow the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain! Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the day of Yahweh comes, for it is close at hand:
echoes.note: 'Blow the trumpet in Zion... for the day of the LORD is coming' associates the trumpet blast with the day of the Lord, the framework for Paul's trumpet and parousia. Continues into 1 Thess 5's 'day of the Lord.'

echoes.text: It will happen in that day that a great trumpet will be blown; and those who were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and those who were outcasts in the land of Egypt, shall come; and they will worship Yahweh in the holy mountain at Jerusalem.
echoes.note: 'a great trumpet will be blown' to gather the scattered to worship the LORD parallels the trumpet summoning the dead and living to meet the Lord. Eschatological-gathering trumpet motif.

echoes.text: For, behold, Yahweh comes out of his place, and will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
echoes.note: 'the LORD is coming forth out of his place, and will come down' provides the descent imagery of God leaving heaven to act, echoed in 'the Lord himself will descend from heaven.' Theophanic descent.

echoes.text: God has gone up with a shout, Yahweh with the sound of a trumpet.
echoes.note: 'God has gone up with a shout, the LORD with the sound of a trumpet' uniquely pairs a loud shout with a trumpet blast, the precise combination in 'with a shout... and with God's trumpet.' Direction is reversed (ascent vs. descent) but the acclamation imagery is striking.

echoes.text: You shall flee by the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains shall reach to Azel; yes, you shall flee, just like you fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Yahweh my God will come, and all the holy ones with you./f + Septuagint reads “him” instead of “you”./f*
echoes.note: 'the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him' parallels 'God will bring with him those who have fallen asleep' and the Lord's coming accompanied by his people. Often cited behind the parousia retinue.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying, “Make two trumpets of silver. You shall make them of beaten work. You shall use them for the calling of the congregation, and for the journeying of the camps. When they blow them, all the congregation shall gather themselves to you at the door of the Tent of Meeting. If they blow just one, then the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather themselves to you. When you blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the […]
echoes.note: The silver trumpets that summon the assembly and signal God's remembrance offer a cultic backdrop to the eschatological trumpet gathering the saints. Faint and thematic.

echoes.text: a day of the trumpet and alarm, against the fortified cities, and against the high battlements.
echoes.note: 'a day of trumpet blast' for the day of the LORD reinforces the trumpet-of-judgment-and-advent motif. Faint, part of the cluster of day-of-the-LORD trumpet texts.

echoes.text: As they still went on, and talked, behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated them; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
echoes.note: Elijah's being 'taken up' bodily to heaven, like Enoch (Gen 5:24), figurally anticipates the living being 'caught up' to meet the Lord without death. Typological rather than verbal.

echoes.text: Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.
echoes.note: Enoch, who 'was not, for God took him,' prefigures the rapture of the living to be with the Lord forever. Faint figural precedent for translation without death.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: For as a young man marries a virgin, so your sons shall marry you; and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
echoes.note: The bridegroom motif organizing the whole parable draws on the prophetic image of God/Messiah as bridegroom: 'as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.' Matthew makes the coming bridegroom the figure for the returning Son of Man, joining the eschatological wedding feast to messianic arrival.

echoes.text: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion. I will even betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know Yahweh.
echoes.note: God's betrothal of Israel ('I will betroth you to me forever') stands behind the bridegroom-and-attendants imagery; the marriage covenant is the controlling metaphor for the eschatological union the wise virgins enter and the foolish miss.

echoes.text: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant? Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel. They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night. King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon. He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of […]
echoes.note: The nocturnal coming of the bridegroom in procession, the cry going up, and the wedding of King Solomon supply a scriptural scene of a bridegroom arriving by night to be met by attendants. Verbal contact is thematic rather than lexical.

echoes.text: “Woe to you who desire the day of Yahweh! Why do you long for the day of Yahweh? It is darkness, and not light. As if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him; Or he went into the house and leaned his hand on the wall, and a snake bit him. Won’t the day of Yahweh be darkness, and not light? Even very dark, and no brightness in it?
echoes.note: The reversal whereby those who presume entry are shut out ('Lord, Lord, open to us' / 'I don't know you') resonates with the prophetic Day of the LORD warning that the day will be darkness for the complacent, not the light they expected.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies. “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap;
echoes.note: 'The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple... but who can endure the day of his coming?' supplies the pattern of a sudden, testing arrival of the Lord for which one must be prepared; the delay-then-sudden-cry structure of the parable echoes this.

echoes.text: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
echoes.note: 'Though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not delay' frames the theme of the bridegroom's delay (v.5) and the call to keep ready through the apparent postponement of the appointed time.
echoes.lxxText: For the vision is yet for a time, and it shall shoot forth at the end, and not in vain: though he should tarry, wait for him; for he will surely come, and will not tarry.

echoes.text: “You shall command the children of Israel, that they bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually. In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it in order from evening to morning before Yahweh: it shall be a statute forever throughout their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.
echoes.note: The provision of pure oil to keep the lamp burning continually 'from evening to morning' supplies the cultic background for oil-as-fidelity that keeps the light alive through the night of waiting.

echoes.text: The princess inside is all glorious. Her clothing is interwoven with gold. She shall be led to the king in embroidered work. The virgins, her companions who follow her, shall be brought to you. With gladness and rejoicing they shall be led. They shall enter into the king’s palace.
echoes.note: The royal wedding psalm, with virgin companions led in procession to the king's palace amid gladness, provides a scriptural template for virgins escorting a bridegroom into the marriage feast.

registers.label: Spare
lines: At midnight the cry went up: the bridegroom is coming!
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
Wisdom is radiant and is found by those who seek her.
We watch for the Lord with longing hearts.
We do not know the day or the hour.
So we keep awake, and keep the oil ready.
Come, let us worship while the lamps still burn.
We come, watching for the Bridegroom. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: It is the middle of the night, the oil running low, the wedding torches guttering — and then a shout splits the dark: the bridegroom is coming, go out to meet him.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
Wisdom is bright and never fades; she is found sitting at the gate by all who rise early to seek her.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
So we watch through the long night, longing, awake, our flasks of oil close at hand.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
We do not know the day or the hour, but we know the One we are waiting for.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
So come, wise and watchful, into the light, and worship.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning. Amen.

lines: At midnight the cry: the bridegroom is here!
